title: Ashok Leyland Posts Record Revenue but Margin Falls a Full Point on Rising Costs
excerpt: India's second-largest CV maker grew Q1 FY27 revenue 10% to ₹10,750 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 10.1% as input costs outpaced sales growth.
body:
• Ashok Leyland's Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 10% to ₹10,750 crore, but EBITDA margin dropped a full percentage point to 10.1%
  • Consolidated profit edged up just 2% to ₹668 crore as rising material and input costs ate into gains from higher volumes
  • The Hinduja Group company posted record commercial vehicle sales for the quarter, with industry-wide retail CV sales up 13.6% to 280,495 units
  • Ashok Leyland approved a £25 million investment in British bus maker Optare Plc as part of its international expansion push

Ashok Leyland delivered record revenue in the June quarter but watched its operating margin slip by a full percentage point, highlighting a tension at the heart of India's second-largest commercial vehicle maker: strong demand is running headlong into rising costs.

The Numbers Tell Two Stories

Consolidated revenue for Q1 FY27 (April–June 2026) rose 10% year-on-year to ₹10,750 crore, driven by record commercial vehicle volumes. On a standalone basis, Reuters reported revenue from operations up 10.4% to ₹9,634 crore, with profit rising 2.3% to ₹609 crore.

But the margin picture was less rosy. EBITDA margin narrowed to 10.1% from 11.1% a year earlier — a 100-basis-point contraction driven by higher material costs. Input costs rose 8.3% during the quarter, pushing total expenses up 11.4% and outpacing revenue growth.

Consolidated net profit came in at ₹668 crore, up just 2% year-on-year — a modest increase that barely kept pace with inflation.

Volume Growth Masked the Margin Squeeze

Industry-wide commercial vehicle retail sales rose 13.6% year-on-year to 280,495 units in the June quarter, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Association (FADA). Ashok Leyland rode that wave with record quarterly CV volumes, though its market share slipped to 17.75% at end-July, down 120 basis points from a year earlier. Tata Motors retained its lead with a 34.85% share.

The company and its peers have implemented price hikes to counter the impact of higher raw material, manufacturing, and freight costs. But the pricing actions have not fully offset the cost surge.

Expansion Continues Despite Margin Pressure

Ashok Leyland is not pulling back on growth spending. The company approved an investment of £25 million ($33.8 million) in British bus maker Optare Plc, signaling continued commitment to international markets.

In FY26, the company reported its strongest-ever annual results: consolidated revenue of ₹44,007 crore and all-time-high commercial vehicle volumes of 220,437 units. Management has guided FY27 capex at a modest ₹750–1,000 crore range and is pursuing selective investments in EV capacity, defence orders, and new product launches including trucks, buses, and LNG vehicles.

"We are happy to report simultaneous increases in market share and operating margins. Our priority remains achieving mid-teen EBITDA margins in the medium term."

— Shenu Agarwal, MD and CEO, Ashok Leyland (on FY26 results)

What Analysts Are Watching

The margin contraction has drawn attention from brokerages. Citi and Nomura both weighed in after the results, with the consensus pointing to a near-term margin recovery hinging on cost-saving initiatives, further price hikes, and a more favorable input cost environment in the second half of FY27.

Ashok Leyland's defence order backlog exceeds ₹1,500 crore, providing revenue visibility. Its EV subsidiary Switch India achieved profit-before-tax breakeven in Q1 FY26 and holds an order book of over 1,500 buses, offering an additional growth lever as India's electric bus adoption accelerates.

The stock is up about 40% over the past year but fell roughly 3% on the day following the earnings release.
author: Diaspora Desk
